questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose a scheduled health check using a non-root user, a systemd timer, and log rotation, mirroring real maintenance tasks.

## Key Concepts
- systemd timer and service pairing
- non-login system users
- logrotate configuration and log hygiene

## Code Example
```bash
# health.sh (as /opt/health/health.sh)
#!/bin/bash
TS=$(date '+%F %T')
OUT="/var/log/health/health.log"
(</dev/tcp/localhost/22) >/dev/null 2>&1; P22=$?
(</dev/tcp/localhost/80) >/dev/null 2>&1; P80=$?
echo "$TS port22=$([ $P22 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED) port80=$([ $P80 -eq 0 ] && echo OPEN || echo CLOSED)" >> "$OUT"
```
```ini
# healthcheck.service
[Unit]
Description=Health check
[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=health
ExecStart=/opt/health/health.sh
```
```ini
# healthcheck.timer
[Unit]
Description=Health check every 5 minutes
[Timer]
OnUnitActiveSec=5min
Unit=healthcheck.service
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
```text
# /etc/logrotate.d/health
 /var/log/health/health.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  missingok
  notifempty
  compress
  delaycompress
  create 0640 health health
 }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test failure handling if the script crashes?
- How could you add alerting for frequent failures?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests SELinux troubleshooting, policy generation, and safe remediation without disabling security controls.

## Key Concepts
- AVCs and audit2allow
- Custom SELinux policy modules
- File context labeling and restorecon
- Validation via audits and controlled writes

## Code Example
```bash
# 1) Identify AVCs from today
ausearch -m avc -ts today | tail
# 2) Create a policy module
ausearch -m avc -ts today | audit2allow -M app_fix
# 3) Load the policy
semodule -i app_fix.pp
# 4) Label directory and content
semanage fcontext -a -t app_data_t '/srv/app/data(/.*)?'
restorecon -R /srv/app/data
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust this if the data directory is on NFS?
- How can you troubleshoot if the policy still blocks legitimate writes after labeling?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

chown root:root "$backup_dir/backup-*.tar.gz"
chmod 600 "$backup_dir/backup-*.tar.gz"
```

```javascript
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf (illustrative)
$DefaultNetstreamDriver gtls
$ActionSendStreamDriver gtls
$TLSCACertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt
$TLSCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/rsyslog-client.crt
$TLSKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/rsyslog-client.key
$ActionSendStreamDriverAuthMode x509/name
$ActionSendStreamDriverPermittedPeer loghub.example.com

# Disk-backed queue configuration
$ActionQueueFileName fwdq1
$ActionQueueMaxDiskSpace 1g
$ActionQueuePersistencyInterval 600
$ActionQueueTimeoutEnqueue 86400
$ActionQueueSaveOnShutdown on

# Forward all application logs
*.* @@loghub.example.com:10514
```

## Verification & Rollback
```bash
# Test configuration syntax
rsyslogd -N1 -f /etc/rsyslog.conf

# Send test log entry
logger "Test TLS forward to loghub.example.com"

# Verify queue status
ls -la /var/spool/rsyslog/

# Rollback: disable forwarding
mv /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf.disabled
systemctl restart rsyslog
```
